question.text: Mr. Vivek Agarwal is setting up 'Deccan Large Value Fund' as a Large Value Fund for Accredited Investors under Cat II AIF. Given LVF status, which IC regulation compliance relief applies?

answer.text: Minimum investor count is reduced from 1,000 to 100
The regulation that IC members shall be responsible for compliance with SEBI (AIF) Regulations is NOT applicable
The fund is exempt from filing any PPM with SEBI
Management fee is capped at 1% instead of 2%

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.7.3, the provision that IC members shall be responsible for SEBI (AIF) Regulation compliance is NOT applicable to Large Value Fund for Accredited Investors. It also doesn't apply to AIFs where each investor has committed minimum INR 70 crore and furnished a waiver. This is the primary LVF IC-governance relief. The Trap: LVF has distinct investor-count and PPM requirements, but not the minimum-investor reduction or PPM exemption stated. Fee caps are not in the LVF regulation. Cross-Exam Context: LVF-specific reliefs tested in XIX-A and XIX-C — including concentration limit (20% instead of 10% per investee). Manager's Pro-Tip: Market LVF as an 'ultra-HNI institutional-grade fund' but document carefully — the LVF reliefs are watched closely during SEBI inspections. Maintain per-investor INR 70 crore commitment evidence in the data room.
